title: France's high school protests
dek: Students blockading their schools over teacher shortages and run-down buildings, the police response, and what the government has promised, from the first blockades in September.
summary: French high school students began blockading their schools in the Paris suburbs in mid to late September, protesting teacher shortages, overcrowded classes, run-down buildings and classrooms that reached 35 to 40°C in heatwaves. Within two weeks the blockades had spread across France, with hundreds of schools closed or disrupted.

The police response has become a story of its own. Thousands of people, most of them minors, have been arrested; hundreds of students, school staff and police officers have been injured. A 15-year-old lost a hand in Lens on October 5, and the government suspended stun grenades at student protests two days later. Rights groups say force against minors has been disproportionate; police unions say force is used against people who attack officers.

The government says students' concerns are legitimate but that the movement is being exploited politically and turned into urban violence. It has promised 3,000 substitute teachers and budget changes; students say that is not enough. A wider national protest day followed on October 17, and unions have called a strike for November 5.

National figures for Saturday's violence rose through Sunday: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez first gave a provisional count of about 1,800 arrests and more than 500 injured police, gendarmes and firefighters, before later counts from CNews and ICI put the toll at nearly 2,400 arrests and roughly 1,000 injured security personnel. Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin told the National Assembly on October 19 that 2,513 people had been taken into custody since the violence, with about two-thirds still held and more than 70 in pre-trial detention; on October 21 he said 174 people had since been jailed and 917 referred to court for prosecution. Prime Minister Lecornu met the mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon on October 22, with no concrete measures announced; the circumstances of the boulevard Magenta death are still being checked. On Saturday, October 24, the interior ministry said 410,000 people (the CGT union says nearly double that) protested nationwide over the cost of living and the school movement, joined by gilets jaunes remnants; police used tear gas and water cannon in Paris and reported nearly 1,000 arrests nationwide, a lower level of violence than the previous weekend.

ground.who: Filmed by a passer-by in a car
ground.shows: A police officer seizes a 15-year-old by the neck and leads him away near a high school in Strasbourg, after the boy asked to get past. The person filming tells the officer to let him go.
ground.label: reported
ground.check: Reported by Paris Match Belgium, which says the clip was shared by the media outlet Shades without context. The date of the incident and any official response are not yet known.

ground.shows: A plainclothes officer holding a 14-year-old girl on the ground in Metz.
ground.label: disputed
ground.check: The girl says she was not assaulted and her guardian has not complained; the officer has filed a defamation complaint, and a police union says he was holding down a struggling teenager (Public Sénat, October 7). The date of the incident is not stated.

phases.name: Blockades begin in the Paris suburbs

events.label: reported
events.text: High school students start blockading school entrances in Créteil, a Paris suburb, over teacher shortages and run-down buildings. Accounts of the exact start date differ; the BBC places the first blockades in the following week.

events.label: reported
events.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez reports 164 arrests in one day, 180 schools affected and 27 people hurt: 12 security officers, 12 students and three school staff. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu says nothing justifies endangering students, staff or police.

events.label: reported
events.text: Education Minister Édouard Geffray meets student leaders and announces a five-point plan. Students say it is not enough.

events.label: reported
events.text: Geffray says 190 students and 78 school staff have been injured and 24 schools burned or ransacked since the movement began, and that about 500 schools are likely to be fully or partly closed the next day.

events.label: disputed
events.text: A 15-year-old loses a hand in an explosion during a protest in Lens. A police union source says he picked up a police grenade to throw it back; prosecutors say it is not yet established whether he picked it up or it landed on him.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: About 250,000 students, teachers and parents protest nationwide, backed by unions, according to the Interior Ministry, which reports 488 arrests and 43 security officers injured.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: A police officer is charged in Paris after a 14-year-old was hit in the face by a tear-gas grenade at close range and lost several teeth.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Nuñez suspends police use of stun grenades at high school protests until the Lens incident is clarified, and says 18 internal investigations into police conduct have been opened. LFI's Manuel Bompard says the suspension came only after children were seriously injured.

events.label: reported
events.text: President Emmanuel Macron holds an emergency meeting with Lecornu and key ministers.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Geffray announces that 3,000 unassigned substitute teachers will be sent to the worst-hit schools.

events.label: reported
events.text: Morocco World News reports the plan also includes extra teaching hours and an online platform for students' demands, and that the Interior Ministry counted 71,500 protesters and 504 arrests that day.

events.label: disputed
events.text: A third week of marches. The Interior Ministry counts 161,500 protesters nationwide, including 41,500 in Paris; unions say about 480,000. Clashes break out near Les Invalides in Paris, and Nuñez says 11 officers were hospitalised.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: After a cabinet meeting, government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon says Macron sees students' concerns as legitimate but believes they are being exploited for political ends and turned into urban violence. He asks ministers for concrete responses within weeks.

events.label: reported
events.text: The Justice Ministry says 7,950 people have been apprehended since late September, 85% of them minors, and 2,735 charged. Lecornu says 248 students, 937 police officers and 149 school staff have been injured. 36 internal investigations into alleged police violence are open.

events.label: reported
events.text: Geffray holds a third meeting with student organisations and says a good part of the way has been made; he says Parcoursup changes due by late October will apply to this year's final-year students. The Union syndicale lycéenne walks out, saying it was not being listened to, and says it will skip a follow-up meeting on Monday.

events.label: reported
events.text: The autumn school holidays begin, which may pause the school blockades.

events.label: reported
events.text: Speaking in Brussels, Macron calls for calm before Saturday's protests, saying the right to protest must come with respect and means not insulting or smashing, and that officers have faced "extreme violence". Prime Minister Lecornu convenes an interministerial crisis cell for Saturday.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez tells France 2 that police and gendarmes must be able to use all their intermediate weapons on Saturday, including stun grenades in case of very serious urban violence.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: The Paris police prefect bans a student march from République to Concorde planned for Saturday, citing serious risks to public order and violence at Tuesday's march. He offers a République–Nation route instead; organisers from Paris-area university assemblies refuse it.

events.label: reported
events.text: Ahead of Saturday's national protest day over the cost of living, joined by students and unions and with online calls from Yellow Vest supporters, Nuñez says he expects about 80 marches to be authorised, with 20,000 to 40,000 people expected in Paris.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Early on Saturday, police disperse small groups attempting to block roads in Lyon, and franceinfo reports burning barricades in Rennes. The main marches, including in Paris, are due in the afternoon.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: In Marseille, France 3 and BFMTV report the first tensions between protesters and police on Saturday morning, with bins set on fire. No official arrest or injury figures have been given yet.

events.label: reported
events.text: The Paris police prefecture tells AFP that about 40 people were arrested early on Saturday, mostly for carrying banned protective gear or weapons, during checks enforcing protest bans near seats of power and train stations. It describes this as a first count.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Before the Paris march leaves Place de la République, franceinfo and CNews report tensions, with police using tear gas; CNews reports projectiles being thrown. No official national figures have been given yet.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: The Interior Minister's office says 166 people had been arrested nationwide by midday; according to AFP, it also counted about 140 actions with 32,800 people outside Paris.

events.label: reported
events.text: The Paris police prefecture says about 20 people were arrested after projectiles were thrown and windows broken outside CNews headquarters. In Marseille, the minister's office says shops were vandalised, and AFP reports protesters briefly entered city hall.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: In Lyon, a branch of the tourism office is ransacked and set on fire during the protest, CNews and ICI report; Al Jazeera cites local media. No official figures for Lyon have been given yet.

events.label: reported
events.text: According to AFP, the Paris police prefecture says about 100 people had been arrested in Paris by midday. Marseille mayor Benoît Payan says President Macron assured him police reinforcements would be sent.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: CNews, ICI and Sud Radio report that 272 people had been arrested nationwide by mid-afternoon; BFM TV gives the count as of 3pm. L'Express, citing Le Parisien, attributes the figure to the interior minister's entourage.

events.label: reported
events.text: The CGT union says more than 500,000 people demonstrated across France, according to franceinfo and ICI. No official turnout figure had been published in the reports seen.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: In Saint-Étienne, a man in his twenties is seriously injured in the hand by a police grenade, AFP reports; the Loire prefecture confirms a serious hand injury, and a source close to the case tells AFP he had picked the grenade up. He was taken to hospital.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: In Lille, protesters force several entrances to the town hall and damage the building before leaving, AFP reports; shops are also looted. Mayor Arnaud Deslandes condemns the acts and says no staff were hurt.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu says the government will not be intimidated and condemns the violence on the margins of the marches; CNews reports he accused the ultra-left of organising it. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez is due to speak in the evening.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: In Bordeaux, people enter and ransack the Gironde prefect's official residence, a prefecture spokesperson tells AFP; city-centre shops are also looted. Prefect Sophie Brocas condemns the damage, and a source close to the authorities tells AFP the RAID police unit was sent in as support.

events.label: reported
events.text: Organisers say about 800,000 people demonstrated across France, franceinfo and ICI report; franceinfo reports the interior minister put the figure at 550,000.

events.label: reported
events.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez says about 550,000 people marched across France, including 110,000 in Paris, and that about 400 people were arrested, Europe 1 reports; CNews also reports 550,000 marchers and at least 400 arrests.

events.label: reported
events.text: In Limoges, a fire breaks out at the town hall after a group attacks the building following the march, Europe 1 reports citing AFP; the prefecture confirms the fire.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: In a post on X, President Emmanuel Macron says there is "no place for violence" in the Republic and that those who damaged or looted prefectures, shops and town halls will be prosecuted and punished; he also voices support for the police.

events.label: reported
events.text: Prime Minister Lecornu rejects La France insoumise leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon's claim that police command was to blame for the chaos in Paris, calling it a dangerous reversal of responsibility, Europe 1 reports citing AFP.

events.label: reported
events.text: The Paris police prefecture says 191 people had been arrested in Paris by 6pm, about 90% of them adults, Europe 1 reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate tells AFP that the Limoges town hall is largely lost: the roof has collapsed onto the lower floors except in the west wing, and about two-thirds of the façade is gone.

events.label: reported
events.text: Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin instructs prosecutors to seek an extremely firm judicial response, including pre-trial detention, for those who attacked police, firefighters, public buildings and shops, Europe 1 reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Late on Saturday, about 30 people try to storm La Santé prison in Paris, firing fireworks mortars at the building and nearby, and four people are arrested, Europe 1 reports.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Visiting security forces in Paris on Saturday evening, Prime Minister Lecornu says about 1,200 people have been arrested across France so far, a higher figure than the interior minister gave earlier in the evening.

events.label: reported
events.text: Lecornu also says 150 police officers and gendarmes were injured, calling it a miracle the toll was not higher, and tells La France insoumise it is now time to choose a side, AFP reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Limoges prosecutor Émilie Abrantes says her office has opened a criminal investigation into the town hall fire, handled by the national police's specialised and organised crime division, and that more than 15 people were in custody on Saturday night, Alouette reports with AFP.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: The mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon ask to meet Prime Minister Lecornu early this week, together with the mayors of other affected towns, and request a detailed and transparent account of how Saturday's events unfolded, Zinfos974 and Lyon Mag report.

events.label: reported
events.text: Paris police say they arrested a record 855 people in the capital over Saturday's violence, and the Paris prosecutor's office says 517 people were in custody on Sunday morning, 346 adults and 171 minors, figures it calls provisional, AFP reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: The Paris police prefecture says a man died following a cardiorespiratory arrest after collapsing on boulevard Magenta, France 24 and L'Express report; both describe him as a demonstrator. The timing and circumstances have not been detailed further.

events.label: reported
events.text: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez gives a provisional national count on Sunday morning of about 1,800 people arrested and more than 500 police officers, gendarmes and firefighters injured, calling the toll provisional, Actu17 reports.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: The national count rises over the course of Sunday: CNews reports 2,397 people arrested nationwide and 997 police officers and gendarmes injured, seven of them seriously, while ICI separately reports close to 2,400 arrests and about a thousand injured security personnel.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu orders partial, localised curfews from Monday night in several cities: central Paris (Place de la République and Les Halles, from 11pm to 6am, with gatherings and demonstrations banned citywide from 8pm), Lyon, Nice and Coulaines, and Lille and three neighbouring communes, some limited to minors; the Bouches-du-Rhône prefecture separately bans all gatherings in Marseille from noon to 8pm. Lecornu rules out a full Paris curfew and says a state of emergency remains possible if needed.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: President Macron declines Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's offer to resign over the weekend's violence, telling him to stay to keep the police chain of command intact. Nuñez says police “lost control” during Saturday's clashes and acknowledges a lack of anticipation and insufficient numbers for the crowds on the fringes of the marches.

events.label: reported
events.text: Interior Minister Gérald Darmanin tells the National Assembly's law committee, during a hearing on the justice ministry's 2027 budget, that 2,513 people have been taken into police custody since Saturday's violence, with about two-thirds still held; more than 70 have been placed in pre-trial detention, 35 of them in the Aix-Marseille area, about 580 are expected to face immediate-appearance hearings in the coming days, and around 50 judicial investigations have been opened, including into the Limoges town hall fire, LCP reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: The mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon will be received by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, at their request, Public Sénat reports; no date has been given for the meeting.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu will receive the mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon on Thursday, October 22, at Matignon, franceinfo and Europe 1 report, setting a date for the meeting the mayors had requested after the October 17 violence.

events.label: reported
events.text: Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin says 174 people have been jailed in connection with the weekend's violence and looting, and that 917 of the roughly 2,500 people taken into custody have been referred to court for prosecution, Europe 1 reports. Separately, the Rhône and Paris prefectures ban planned Thursday marches by student groups, and the Perpignan prefecture bans demonstrations in its city centre from October 22 to 25.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Prime Minister Lecornu meets union leaders at Matignon for two and a half hours, Euronews and Public Sénat report, but high-school and student unions are not invited, which the CFDT and CGT say they regret. CGT leader Sophie Binet says the government announced no measures responding to the protests and gave no consideration to unions' demands; CFTC leader Cyril Chabanier calls the meeting disappointing but says the government opened the door to discussing a minimum-wage rise.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: The CGT and other unions call for a nationwide mobilisation on November 5, with Binet urging workers to extend the action into a strike from that date, Euronews and Public Sénat report. Separately, gilets jaunes groups plan a cost-of-living protest in Paris and other cities on Saturday, October 24, which the CGT's Paris branch says it will join, Public Sénat and The Connexion report.

events.label: confirmed
events.text: Prime Minister Lecornu receives the mayors of Paris, Marseille and Lyon at Matignon on Thursday as they had requested after the October 17 violence; the mayors had asked for a precise, transparent account of how that day's events unfolded. BFM TV and Le Progrès report no concrete measures were announced. Lyon mayor Grégory Doucet says afterwards he expects Saturday's planned demonstration in his city to be allowed to go ahead.

events.label: reported
events.text: Police ban student marches planned for Thursday in Paris, Lyon, Lille and Grenoble, citing the risk of further violence after the previous weekend's unrest. After a security meeting at the Élysée, Macron says protests organised by groups with "no legitimate authority" will not be tolerated and that there should be no demonstrations in the coming days, blaming radical far-left groups and opportunistic looters for the violence; a Paris administrative court later overturns the capital's ban after organisers challenge it, AP reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: President Macron meets high-school student representatives at the Élysée on Friday, for the first time since the protest movement began over five weeks ago. The student representatives call afterward to keep up the mobilisation, France24 reports; the meeting's outcome and any concessions have not been detailed in reports seen.

events.label: reported
events.text: At the meeting, Higher Education Minister Philippe Baptiste rules out abolishing the Parcoursup university admissions platform, calling that "pure demagoguery," but says he is open to "profound changes." The government points again to the promised 3,000 substitute teachers and an extra €1.1 billion for education in the 2027 budget, and sets a further meeting for Monday, October 26, when it says it will present a first set of decisions on staffing, teacher replacements and Parcoursup, Al Jazeera reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Student representatives, including Soumaya Sarre of the Fédération des Lycéens des Quartiers Populaires and Nathanaël Combary of Renouveau Lycéen, say years of unkept promises make them wary, and call for commitments backed by results. Combary names an overhaul of Parcoursup and a €1.5 billion emergency plan for school buildings as priorities, while other groups seek €10 billion more for education, more permanent teachers and 250,000 extra university places, Al Jazeera reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: The interior ministry says 410,000 people protested nationwide on Saturday, including 110,000 in Paris, in marches over the cost of living and the high-school movement; the CGT union puts both figures at nearly double the official count. In Paris, authorities bar the originally negotiated central route, leaving only a march from Porte d'Italie to Porte de Vincennes on the city's south-eastern edge; protests are also banned in Montpellier, Rouen, Nice and central Lyon, while a union march is authorised in Marseille under strict conditions. More than 70,000 police and gendarmes are deployed, including the RAID unit, at least 24 Paris metro stations are closed, and the Louvre and Musée d'Orsay shut for the day, Al Jazeera reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Police use tear gas and water cannon in Paris as the mood turns tense towards nightfall; authorities say about 500 "rioters" clashed with police, a lower level of violence than the previous weekend. Police also use tear gas on about 150 protesters in Lyon, and clashes are reported in Marseille. Police say nearly 1,000 people have been arrested nationwide, including 65 in Paris earlier in the day, Al Jazeera reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: Remnants of the 2018 gilets jaunes cost-of-living movement join Saturday's protests, as unions had said they would; the movement separately announces a further protest for the following Saturday, October 31, Al Jazeera reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: The government announces it will cancel the 836 secondary-education post cuts planned in the 2027 budget and add 500 teaching posts in public lycées, AFP reports via La Dernière Heure and LCP. Higher Education Minister Philippe Baptiste says Parcoursup will be strongly changed from the 2027 intake before being replaced in 2028, which needs a law passed by Parliament.

events.label: reported
events.text: The announcements also include 15,000 extra higher-education places, a €5 billion renovation plan for lycées and universities (mostly low-rate loans to local authorities), student grants indexed to inflation and a cap of 28 pupils in seconde classes, AFP reports. Education Minister Édouard Geffray says none of the decisions is "an empty promise".

events.label: reported
events.text: French student and pupil organisations say the government's October 26 education measures fall short and vow to keep mobilising, AFP reports. The Union étudiante calls them "largely insufficient", UNEF says the government is answering with "crumbs", and the Snes-FSU teachers' union says youth demands are not met and urges a stronger strike ahead of November 5; the youth bodies' platform asks for 10 measures costing €10 billion.

events.label: reported
events.text: More than 300,000 people join a new wave of protests on Saturday, smaller than the mid-October unrest, Bloomberg reports; in Paris, where about 70,000 officers were deployed, police arrest 779 people and five officers are injured. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez calls a Molotov cocktail attack on an officer "attempted murder", and an investigation has been opened, according to AFP.

events.label: reported
events.text: Student unions call for school blockades this week and urge students to join the cross-sector strike on November 5, Bloomberg reports.

events.label: reported
events.text: France: about 15,000 people marched in Rennes on October 31 against the cost of living and in support of the school students' movement, Ouest-France reports. Local unions say they will keep their November 5 march route despite a prefectural ban.

events.label: disputed
events.text: France: officials said 48 of the country's 3,700 high schools and 51 of 184 higher-education institutions were disrupted on November 3, while the USL student union put the number of blocked schools at about 500 and the Union Étudiante said over 50 campuses were blockaded. The USL denounced riot police deployed outside schools; Education Minister Édouard Geffray said on X that blockades deprive students of their right to an education. A nationwide union strike is set for November 5.

events.label: reported
events.text: France: unions say a nationwide strike on November 5 is shaping up to be large, with the CGT counting 1,140 strike notices across its organisations, Ouest-France reports. In Rennes, local unions have counted 45 specific strike calls across sectors, from rail to health and education, and want to keep their march route despite the prefecture's ban.

events.label: disputed
events.text: France: the education ministry counted 40 of 3,700 high schools blocked on Monday, while the USL student union claimed 196, Le Monde reports. Minister Édouard Geffray called the blockades "clearly residual"; the heads' union SNPDEN-UNSA counted 35 schools in Paris alone blocked in whole or part on Tuesday. The ministry has not said what its figure covers.

events.label: reported
events.text: France: ahead of the November 5 strike, the towns of Romans-sur-Isère and Valence say they will keep schools open for pupils where at least 25% of teachers strike, with canteens closed and children bringing their own meals, ici (Radio France) reports. Unions plan marches in Valence and Montélimar, and rallies across Ardèche; pupils plan early blockades outside several high schools in the area.

events.label: reported
events.text: Unions have listed 45 specific strike calls across sectors ahead of the November 5 protest in Rennes and say they will keep the march route despite a prefectural ban. Ouest‑France reports the unions expect a larger turnout than the 15,000 demonstrators who marched on October 31.

events.label: pending
events.text: Turnout and outcome of the unions' November 5 interprofessional strike and demonstration, whether the government's October 26 commitments are funded and legislated, a reconciled national custody and prosecution total, the boulevard Magenta death inquiry, and the findings of the roughly 50 judicial investigations opened since October 17. Still being checked.

claims.title: Who is driving the movement?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: The government says students' concerns are legitimate but that the movement is being exploited for political ends and turned into urban violence.
claims.b: Students describe it as a response to teacher shortages, overcrowding and neglected buildings. LFI, which the government has blamed for stoking tensions, says the government acted on police force only after children were badly hurt.
claims.status: Open. Both positions are on record; there is no independent finding on who organises the protests.

claims.title: How did the Lens student lose his hand?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: A police union source says the 15-year-old picked up a police grenade and tried to throw it back.
claims.b: Prosecutors say investigators have not established whether he picked it up or it landed on him, or whether the shot followed the rules. The grenade model was suspended as a precaution.
claims.status: Under investigation by police internal affairs.

claims.title: How many marched on October 13?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: The Interior Ministry counted 161,500 people nationwide, including 41,500 in Paris.
claims.status: Both figures are reported; no independent count is available.

claims.title: Has police force been proportionate?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: Amnesty International France says policing must be lawful, necessary and proportionate, and has criticised force against minors. A lawyer for arrested students says every client she represents reports being insulted, slapped, held down or put in chokeholds.
claims.b: The Alliance police union says force is justified against people who attack officers and rejects the word repression. The Interior Minister has condemned violence against police.
claims.status: 36 internal investigations into alleged police violence are open (Interior Ministry, October 14).

claims.title: Is the government's response enough?
claims.label: disputed
claims.a: The government has promised 3,000 substitute teachers for the worst-hit schools, extra teaching hours, a consultation platform and budget changes; Geffray says 2,000 substitutes had started by October 14.
claims.b: Students say the measures are insufficient and have called for protests to join the October 17 national day.
claims.status: Macron has asked ministers for concrete responses within weeks.

turnout.title: How many marched, by whose count
turnout.caption: The union figure is the organisers' own count. Sources: Interior Ministry and unions, via Euronews and AFP. No independent count is available.
turnout.aria: Turnout: about 250,000 on October 6 per the Interior Ministry; on October 13, 161,500 per the ministry and about 480,000 per unions

injuries.title: People injured since late September, per the Prime Minister
injuries.caption: As of October 14. Source: Sébastien Lecornu, via AFP. Figures for students have varied by ministry and date.
injuries.aria: Injured as of October 14 per the Prime Minister: 937 police officers, 248 students, 149 school staff

arrests.title: Arrests since late September, per the Justice Ministry
arrests.caption: As of October 14, 85% of them minors. Source: Justice Ministry, via AFP. Euronews cites 6,800 taken into custody.
arrests.aria: As of October 14: 7,950 people apprehended and 2,735 charged, per the Justice Ministry

gaps: A single reconciled national total for arrests and injuries from the October 17 violence (figures rose through the day, from about 1,800 arrests/500 injured to about 2,400 arrests/1,000 injured). Also: a precise current custody count, the circumstances of the death of a man who collapsed on boulevard Magenta in Paris, whether an investigation is opened into the Saint-Étienne injury, progress in the Limoges town hall fire investigation, and an independent account of the La Santé prison incident
What concessions, if any, follow Friday's Élysée meeting between Macron and student representatives, and the Paris administrative court's reasoning for overturning the Thursday protest ban

A reconciled national arrest and injury total for Saturday October 24's protests, and the official turnout for the October 31 protests (Bloomberg reported more than 300,000 people), and the outcome of the November 5 union mobilisation
Findings of the roughly 50 judicial investigations opened since October 17, and of the earlier 36 internal police investigations
Outcomes of the roughly 580 immediate-appearance hearings Darmanin says are expected
Whether all 3,000 substitute teachers are in place
The government's concrete proposals, requested by Macron within weeks
Exact date and school where the first blockade began

corrections.text: The October 8 entry on substitute teachers was labelled confirmed, but only the 3,000-teacher figure was reported by two independent outlets. The extra teaching hours, the online platform and that day's turnout and arrest figures came from one outlet; they are now a separate entry labelled reported.
